The Lawanti Community Development Foundation has demanded an independent investigation and prosecution of Nigerian Air Force personnel over the alleged killing of three residents and shooting of 11 others in Lawanti, Akko North Local Council Development Area of Gombe State. The foundation, which accused personnel of the 109 Combat Reconnaissance Base of opening fire on residents on November 20, also demanded compensation for the families of the deceased and injured victims. In a statement issued on Monday and signed by its Executive Director and Programme Manager, the foundation condemned what it described as an act of brutality and indiscriminate shooting, insisting that the community would pursue justice through lawful means. According to the foundation, “the incident began following an allegation by Air Force personnel that an electrical cable connected to a transformer within their facility near the Gombe Airport had been stolen.” It said the personnel reported the matter to the District Head of Lawanti, who reportedly assured them of the community’s cooperation in identifying those responsible. However, the foundation alleged that military personnel later invaded the community around 7pm, assaulting residents, intimidating traders and forcing businesses to close. The development reportedly triggered protests along the Gombe-Bauchi Highway, where residents barricaded sections of the road with burning tyres. The foundation said calm was eventually restored following the intervention of the Emir of Gona, the Chairman of Akko North LCDA and other community stakeholders. The deceased have since been buried in accordance with Islamic rites, while the 11 survivors are receiving treatment for varying degrees of injuries, the statement added. Expressing outrage over the incident, the foundation said, “No stolen cable, regardless of its value, can ever be worth the life of a single innocent Nigerian.” It added, “Even where a crime has been committed, the responsibility of security personnel is to investigate, identify suspects and ensure that justice takes its lawful course, not to subject an entire community to collective punishment.” The foundation stressed that its condemnation of the alleged shootings should not be mistaken for hostility towards the military, noting that residents respected the sacrifices of the armed forces in defending the country. It must never become an instrument of oppression against the very citizens it is meant to protect,” it said. It also warned against a situation in which civilians could allegedly be assaulted or killed without accountability because those involved wore military uniforms. The community commended Governor Muhammadu Yahaya for condemning the incident, ordering an investigation and dispatching a government delegation led by the Secretary to the State Government, Professor Ibrahim Abubakar Njodi, to engage with affected residents. It also acknowledged the governor’s pledge to provide medical and humanitarian assistance to the injured and bereaved families but urged him to ensure that the investigation resulted in concrete action. Among its demands, the foundation called for an independent commission of inquiry, with civilian representation, to investigate the incident and make its findings public. It also urged the Chief of the Air Staff and the Minister of Defence to identify personnel involved in the alleged operation and ensure that those found culpable were prosecuted. The foundation further called on the National Human Rights Commission to investigate the alleged extrajudicial killings, indiscriminate shootings and other human rights violations. It demanded adequate compensation for the families of the three deceased residents and the survivors, as well as comprehensive medical treatment and rehabilitation for the injured at no personal cost. The community also sought guarantees against intimidation or reprisals targeting victims, eyewitnesses and community leaders. Reiterating its commitment to peace, the foundation urged youths in Lawanti to remain calm and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions. “We will pursue every lawful and constitutional avenue available to ensure that the deaths of our three community members are not swept under the carpet and that the injured receive the justice and support they deserve,” the statement added. It called on civil society organisations, human rights groups and the media to support its demand for justice, declaring that the lives of Lawanti residents must not be treated as expendable.
